windows: RAM: press Ctrl+Shift+Esc, open Performance, then Memory.
GPU memory (VRAM): Performance, then GPU, then "Dedicated GPU memory". With an NVIDIA card you can also run `nvidia-smi` in PowerShell. No dedicated GPU? Enter 0.
Free disk: open File Explorer, then This PC, and read the space under your C: drive.
macos: RAM: Apple menu, then About This Mac. On Apple Silicon this memory is shared with the GPU, so you can enter the same number as VRAM.
Free disk: Apple menu, System Settings, General, Storage.
Intel Mac without a dedicated GPU? Enter 0 for VRAM.
linux: RAM: run `free -h` and read the "total" column.
GPU memory (VRAM): run `nvidia-smi` for NVIDIA cards. No dedicated GPU? Enter 0.
Free disk: run `df -h ~` and read the "Avail" column.

steps.title: Install Ollama
steps.explain: Ollama is the free program that downloads and runs open-source AI models on your own computer. You install it once and it works for every model.

notes.windows: Open PowerShell as Administrator first: press Start, type PowerShell, right-click it and choose Run as administrator. Prefer a normal installer? Download it from https://ollama.com/download instead.
notes.macos: No Homebrew? Download the Ollama app from https://ollama.com/download, move it into Applications and open it once. In that case you can skip this command and just paste anything to continue, or press Skip.
notes.linux: The script may ask for your password (sudo). Nothing appears while you type it. That is normal.

steps.expected: The command finishes without red error text. Paste whatever the terminal printed.
steps.success_message: Looks fine. The next step is the real test.

steps.title: Check that Ollama is installed
steps.explain: Close your terminal and open a new one so it notices the fresh install. Then ask Ollama for its version.
steps.expected: A line such as: ollama version is 0.x.x

success_notes.message: The warning only means the Ollama server is not running yet. The next step checks it.

steps.title: Make sure the Ollama server is running
steps.explain: Ollama works quietly in the background and answers on port 11434. This check asks whether it is awake.

notes.windows: If it fails, open the Ollama app from the Start menu, wait about 10 seconds and try again.
notes.macos: If it fails, open the Ollama app, or run `brew services start ollama`, or run `ollama serve` in a second terminal and leave it open.
notes.linux: If it fails, run `sudo systemctl start ollama`, or run `ollama serve` in a second terminal and leave it open.

steps.title: Download the model: {tag}
steps.explain: This downloads the model files ({size}). It can take several minutes depending on your internet. Progress bars are normal.

notes.default: You can stop with Ctrl+C and run the same command later. The download resumes where it stopped.

steps.expected: The output ends with the word: success

steps.title: Confirm the model is on your computer
steps.explain: This lists every model stored on your machine.
steps.expected: A table with a row for {tag}.

steps.title: Talk to the model
steps.explain: Ask {tag} a question straight from the terminal. The first run loads the model into memory, so it can take a little while.

notes.default: For a back-and-forth chat run `ollama run {tag}` instead, and type `/bye` to leave.

steps.expected: A short answer in plain English.
steps.success_message: It works. You are running an open-source AI model on your own computer.

steps.title: Optional: check the local API
steps.explain: Your own programs can talk to the model through this local address. This is how apps like this one use Ollama.
steps.success_message: The local API answers and knows your model.

steps.title: Optional: check Python
steps.explain: If you want to use the model from your own code, you need Python 3.10 or newer.
steps.expected: Python 3.10 or newer, for example Python 3.12.4

steps.title: Optional: check Git
steps.explain: Git lets you download and share code projects.
steps.expected: A line such as: git version 2.45.0
